subject: Finova - Decision criteria clarification (latency / cost / SLA) - follow-up
thread_summary: Post-demo follow-up to clarify Finova's decision criteria (latency targets, cost expectations, deployment mode, and SLA requirements), gather stakeholder mapping (economic buyer, security, procurement), and agree next steps for procurement and a technical feasibility call.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:10:00Z
Subject: Finova - Decision criteria recap & ask (latency / cost / SLA)

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and a few clarifying asks so we can prepare the right technical and commercial packaging.

Recap:
- Core use case: low-latency, high-throughput inference for customer-facing assistants (short prompts, single-turn and multi-turn).
- Primary concerns you flagged: p95 latency, per-token cost, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and SLA/uptime requirements.
- Current timeline: procurement review targeted for end of March.

Asks / clarifying questions:
1) Latency target: you mentioned wanting "sub-100ms p95" in some cases — can you confirm whether that is an absolute requirement for all traffic, or for a specific slice?
2) Cost target: do you have a target $/token or monthly spend range we should design around?
3) Deployment constraint: will you require private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for any of this workload due to PII/data residency, or would Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) suffice?
4) SLA: do you require a 99.9% or higher uptime SLA, and are there specific recovery time objectives (RTO) or penalties we should be aware of?
5) Stakeholder mapping: can you confirm the economic buyer and introduce security/procurement contacts so we can route the SOC2/KMS audit info and initial SOW?

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm the above, we can get a quick SOW draft + rough cost model over to procurement and a technical brief to security. Rishi (cc'd) will put together a latency/cost estimate for dedicated vs private.

Thanks — appreciate the quick confirmation on the three bullets above so we can move the procurement conversation forward.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

---
Attachment: redwood_sla_summary.pdf (summary of standard SLA tiers)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: 2026-02-20T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria recap & ask (latency / cost / SLA)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side: we spoke with Product/Platform after the call.

1) Latency: sub-100ms p95 is desirable for the high-priority customer flows (search-assist and checkout help). For lower-priority background flows, p95 ~200ms is acceptable. If you can show a path to sub-100ms for a subset of traffic that would be ideal.
2) Cost: we're looking to keep immediate variable costs under ~$0.002/token for the hosted equivalent; we understand dedicated/private will change unit economics.
3) Deployment: for PII-containing requests we will need private (VPC) deployment. For other traffic, Dedicated would be preferred to balance cost and performance.
4) SLA: Product wants >=99.9% for the high-priority flows, Finance will push for penalties in enterprise contract language.

Stakeholders:
- Economic buyer: Marcus Liu, VP Product (marcus.liu@finova.com) — primary for feature/budget signoff.
- Security: Sofia Rivera (sofia.r@finova.com) — I'll loop her into this thread.
- Procurement: procurement@finova.com — copied.

I'll introduce Marcus and Sofia in a separate email shortly. Procurement is tracking to a decision by the end of March, as you noted.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Product Manager, Finova
alex.j@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finova.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@finova.com>

Date: 2026-02-22T11:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria recap & ask (latency / cost / SLA)

Alex / Marcus — thanks for confirming. Quick follow-ups before Rishi does a technical estimate:
- Can you confirm expected monthly token volume (ballpark is fine: e.g., 100M, 500M, 1B tokens) so we can size Dedicated capacity vs burst?
- For the private/VPC requirement, is that for all PII traffic only or do you expect entire tenant isolation (all traffic) to be in scope?
- Any specific compliance docs you need up front (SOC 2 report, encryption attestations, penetration test report)? We have SOC2 Type II and can provide encryption/KMS details and an audit log export sample.

Rishi (cc) will propose 2 configurations: Dedicated with strict routing rules + prefix caching for mixed traffic, and a Private VPC option for PII. We'll call out expected p95 ranges and cost delta.

If it's helpful, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute sync with Marcus/Sofia + Rishi next week.

Best,
Marissa

From: Sofia Rivera <sofia.r@finova.com>

Date: 2026-02-23T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria recap & ask (latency / cost / SLA)

Hi Marissa / Alex — thanks for looping me in. A few security specifics to help you size the Private/Dedicated options:

- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report required; we will need to review.
- Data protection: encryption at rest + KMS integration required for any PII workloads.
- Auditability: immutable audit logs with 90-day retention for initial deployment (longer-term retention may be needed).
- Data residency: any EU customer data must remain in EU region. For US-only initial pilots that is not a blocker.
- Pen tests: we may request a recent penetration test report or allowlist for our security team to run scans.

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to complete vendor selection and SOW execution by March 31. Please send SOC2 and encryption/KMS docs to procurement@finova.com and cc me.

Thanks,
Sofia Rivera
Head of Security Engineering, Finova
sofia.r@finova.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@finova.com>, Sofia Rivera <sofia.r@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria recap & ask (latency / cost / SLA)

Thanks for the details — wrote up a short technical note and attached a rough latency/cost model. High-level takeaways: 

- Deployment modes:
  * Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant): lowest operational lift, higher unit cost, not acceptable for PII.
  * Dedicated: isolated GPU pools, predictable p95 latency (we can target ~110-130ms p95 for short prompts under steady load with per-customer caching and batching optimizations).
  * Private (VPC): gives full network isolation and KMS control; sub-100ms p95 is possible but depends on on-prem/colocated hardware and network path — typically requires closer network topology to your app tier.

- Cost delta: Dedicated expected to be ~20-40% cheaper than hosted for high volume; Private has higher fixed setup cost but can lower long-run unit cost if you commit capacity.

- For your stated needs (subset of traffic needing sub-100ms; PII on private), recommended approach: route high-priority flows to a colocated/private deployment (or Dedicated in the same cloud region with reserved capacity) and use Dedicated for the rest. This balances cost and SLA.

I attached a simple spreadsheet with token-tier cost estimates and two latency scenario projections.

Happy to run a short benchmark with a sample prompt set if you can provide ~1k representative requests.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
